must_identify.text: The five Suricata detections are treated as one scanning activity in one thread: a single internal source (198.51.100.25) sending SYN probes to several hosts (192.0.2.14, 192.0.2.31, 192.0.2.52) on several ports.

The hypothesis of hostile internal reconnaissance gets the verdict refuted, and the reason given is that the alerts match the recon delta's scheduled run from corpscan03 on all three points: the source is corpscan03's address 198.51.100.25, every alert falls inside the run's 02:00:00Z to 02:41:37Z span on 2026-07-28, and every destination port is in the run's scanned port set.
The brief notes that nothing in the intake goes past scanning: no exploit or post-scan signature, and no detection on any of the scanned hosts.

Confidence is Medium, and the brief names analyst confirmation that corpscan03 is the lab's sanctioned scanner and that its recon-weekly-tcp schedule is real as what would raise it; the recon delta's own account of the run is treated as telemetry, not as confirmed environment context.

A data request or investigate option asks for confirmation of the scanner and its schedule from a source outside the alerts (the scan job's configuration or schedule, or the analyst who owns corpscan03).
A tuning option excludes the scheduled scanner (its source address, optionally limited to the run's schedule) from the scan rules, rather than disabling the rules.

must_not.text: The brief does not call the activity a confirmed attack, a compromise, or confirmed hostile reconnaissance.
No option recommends isolating, blocking or shutting down corpscan03 or its address 198.51.100.25.
No option recommends disabling, deleting or suppressing the scan rules (100901, 100902, 100903, or SIDs 1000101 to 1000103) for every source.
